chief_complaint: sudden fever, severe body aches, sore throat, and cough
hpi_details: A 35-year-old male presents to the clinic with sudden fever, severe body aches, sore throat, and cough. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he caught a severe strain of COVID-19 or got pneumonia from getting drenched during a rainy commute.
concerns: He is worried that he will pass the illness to his pregnant wife who has asthma.
expectations: He hopes to get a rapid swab test to know what it is and a medical sick note for his employer for the rest of the week.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Influenza is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Influenza: Rest, hydration, Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) if within 48 hours, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden fever, severe body aches, sore throat, and cough

Key HPI features: A 35-year-old male presents to the clinic with sudden fever, severe body aches, sore throat, and cough. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 39.0C, HR 96, BP 118/76, RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air. Pharyngeal erythema without exudate, mild cervical lymphadenopathy, lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Rapid influenza PCR/antigen test positive for Influenza A.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Influenza.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to COVID-19 without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe breathlessness or chest pain — suggests complication like pneumonia.
management_principles: Plan for Influenza: Rest, hydration, Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) if within 48 hours
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: sudden fever, severe body aches, sore throat, and cough

A 35-year-old male presents to the clinic with sudden fever, severe body aches, sore throat, and cough. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 39.0C, HR 96, BP 118/76, RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air. Pharyngeal erythema without exudate, mild cervical lymphadenopathy, lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Rapid influenza PCR/antigen test positive for Influenza A.
reference_soap.assessment: Influenza A, uncomplicated, based on positive rapid antigen/PCR testing and consistent clinical picture (acute fever, myalgia, sore throat, cough).
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Influenza: Rest, hydration, Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) if within 48 hours. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Influenza
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Influenza
Implement evidence-based management plan: Rest, hydration, Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) if within 48 hours

teaching.one_liner: A viral respiratory infection causing sudden fever, severe body aches, sore throat, and cough — antivirals like oseltamivir help most if started within 48 hours.
red_flags: Severe breathlessness or chest pain — suggests complication like pneumonia

must_ask.say: Did the fever and body aches come on suddenly?
Do you have body aches, sore throat, and cough together?
How many days have you had symptoms?
Did you get a flu shot this year?

history.answer: I suddenly came down with a high fever, severe body aches, a sore throat, and a cough yesterday.
The fever started very abruptly yesterday morning, about thirty hours ago, and it has stayed high since.
I measured thirty-nine degrees Celsius at home, and I have been shivering with intense chills.
I took two acetaminophen pills last night, but my fever only dropped a little bit for a few hours before spiking back up.
I have a dry, hacking cough and a raw sore throat, but I haven't coughed up any phlegm.
No, I am not short of breath, and I don't feel any chest pain when I breathe in.
No, I don't have any pain or burning when I urinate, and I am not urinating more often.
No, I haven't had any stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
I have a generalized dull headache from the high fever, but my neck doesn't feel stiff at all.
My muscles and back ache severely all over, but I have not had any joint swelling, rash, or bug bites.
I sweat when the fever fluctuates, but I have not had chronic night sweats or any unexplained weight loss.
I noticed a couple of small, slightly tender lumps along the sides of my neck this morning, but none in my armpits or groin.
No, I haven't traveled overseas recently, haven't been hiking or doing farm work, and haven't touched any animals.
A couple of my coworkers at my office came down with influenza earlier this week.
No, I have never had cancer treatment, taken steroids, or taken medications that suppress the immune system.
No, I don't have any heart disease or artificial valves, and I haven't had any dental procedures recently.
No, I haven't started any new prescription medications or supplements lately.
I am married in a monogamous relationship, and I have never used injection drugs.
No, I haven't gotten the seasonal influenza vaccine this year.
Since my fever started just yesterday, I wanted to see a doctor quickly to see if there is antiviral medicine I can take.
I thought maybe I caught COVID-19 or came down with pneumonia after walking home in the freezing rain.
I'm really worried that I might pass this terrible fever and cough to my pregnant wife, especially since she has asthma.
I have always been healthy, with no chronic conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or asthma.
None, I have never had any surgeries or been admitted to a hospital.
None, I don't take any regular daily medications.
No, I don't have any known allergies to medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink socially, having a beer once or twice a month at most.
I work as an office worker and live with my wife in an apartment.
Both of my parents are alive and healthy, and there are no major diseases in my family.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 96 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 39.0°C, oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
The patient appears acutely ill, febrile, and fatigued, but is alert and in no acute respiratory distress.
Erythematous posterior pharynx without tonsillar enlargement, exudate, or petechiae.
Both tympanic membranes are pearly gray, translucent, and intact with normal light reflexes.
Mild bilateral anterior cervical lymphadenopathy with slight tenderness on palpation; no posterior cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal vesicular breath sounds and no crackles, wheezes, or rhonchi.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender without voluntary guarding or muscular rigidity.
No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly palpated below the costal margins.
No costovertebral angle tenderness elicited on gentle percussion bilaterally.
Skin is warm and flushed without rash, petechiae, purpura, or tick bites.
Neck is supple with full range of motion; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
